children.text: Chapter 1

atitatīvrātitīvrataraviśṛṅkhalaśaktipātāghrātasya svasvarūpasamāviṣṭasya kasyacit kvacit kadācit akasmād eva mahāsāhasavṛttyā ghasmaramahāghanataraparanādollāsasphāreṇa savikalpanirvikalpātmakasamastasaṃvinnivahaghaṭṭanān nirāvaraṇamahāśūnyatāsamāveśaniṣṭhayā svarūpalābhaḥ samastakalpanottīrṇatvād akṛtakaniravakāśaniruttaranistaraṅganiravadhinirniketāsparśasaṃvitprāptir bhavati iti rahasyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The secret meaning is this: for someone, somewhere, at some time, who has been touched by an exceedingly intense, indeed still more intense and unrestrained <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power), and who has entered his own true form, there suddenly arises, through the activity of great audacity, through the expansive swelling of the devouring, very dense supreme sound, and through the striking together of the whole mass of consciousness consisting of both determinate and indeterminate cognition, the attainment of his own nature, grounded in entry into the unobstructed great void. Because he has gone beyond all conceptual construction, there comes the attainment of consciousness that is unmade, without aperture, unsurpassed, waveless, limitless, without fixed abode, and untouched.

children.text: mahāsāhasavṛttyānupraveśaś ca vakṣyamāṇakathitakrameṇādhigantavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the entrance through the activity of great audacity is to be understood according to the sequence that will be described below.

children.text: jhaṭiti sarvollaṅghanakrameṇāniketasvarūpaprāptisākṣātkāramahāsāhasacarcāsampradāyaṃ nirūpya idānīṃ tatraiva sarvavṛttimahāsāmarasyam ekakāle pracakṣate ||
children.translated_text: Having explained the tradition of discourse on the great audacity that is the direct realization of attaining the form without fixed abode, by the process of instantly overleaping everything, he now teaches, in that very context, the great complete fusion of all activities at one and the same time.

children.text: Chapter 2

vṛttīnāṃ dṛgādimarīcirūpāṇāṃ tathā rāgadveṣādyunmeṣavatīnāṃ yugapat tulyakālaṃ kramaparipāṭyullaṅghanena akramapravṛttyā tallābhācchuritā tat tena prāguktamahāsāhasadaśāsamāveśakramaprāpyeṇa svarūpalābhena kālākālakalpanottīrṇālaṃgrāsavapuṣā mahānirīheṇācchuritā spṛṣṭā svasvarūpatāṃ nītā pravṛttiḥ prakarṣeṇa vartamānā vṛttiḥ satatam acyutatayā tatsamāveśenāvasthānam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The activity of the functions, which have the form of rays such as seeing and the like, and likewise of those that arise as passion, aversion, and so on, is simultaneous, at the same time. By overleaping the ordered sequence and operating without sequence, it is tinged by that attainment; that is, it is tinged, touched, and led to its own true nature by the attainment of one's own form that is reached through entry into the previously mentioned state of great audacity, whose body completely swallows the conceptualization of time and non-time, and which is greatly free from effort. The meaning is that the function, intensely present, remains constantly and unfailingly through entry into that state.

children.text: ity anayā uktibhaṅgyā sarvavṛttīnāṃ samanantaram eva sarvottīrṇamahāśūnyatādhāmni dhāmarūpe tanmayatayā parasparavibhedavigalanena udayapadavyām eva satatam avasthitiḥ sthitety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this manner of expression it is meant that all the functions, immediately and constantly, remain in the path of arising itself, in the abode that is the realm of the all-transcending great void, by becoming identical with it and by the dissolution of their mutual differences.

children.text: ity anayā uktibhaṅgyā tulyakālakathanopadeśam uktvā idānīṃ pustakakathāṃ nirūpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Having stated, by this manner of expression, the instruction that speaks of simultaneity, they now explain the account of the book.

children.text: Chapter 3
śrīmanniṣkriyānandanāthānugrahasamaye śrīgandhamādanasiddhapādair akṛtakapustakapradarśanena yā parapade prāptir upadiṣṭā saiva vitatya nirūpyate ||
children.translated_text: At the time of the grace of glorious <s>Niṣkriyānandanātha</s>, through glorious <s>Gandhamādanasiddhapāda</s>'s showing of the unmade book, the attainment of the supreme state was taught; that very teaching is now explained in detail.

children.text: saptarandhrakramoditasaptaśikhollāsātmakaḥ prāṇapravāhodayaḥ sa evordhvapaṭṭakaḥ pūrṇavṛttyudayaḥ randhradvayasuṣiranālikāpravāhaprasṛto 'pānarūpo 'dhaḥpaṭṭakaḥ pañcendriyaśaktiveṣṭitaḥ pañcaphaṇadharmānibandhako 'dhaḥsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The arising of the current of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), whose nature is the flashing forth of seven flames arisen in sequence from the seven apertures, is itself the upper band, the arising of the full function. The lower band, in the form of <s>apāna</s>, extends as the flow through the hollow channel of the two apertures, is enveloped by the powers of the five senses, binds the condition of the five hoods, and is situated below.

children.text: tasya valayadvayaṃ jāgratsvapnātmakam unmudrya granthinibandhanam apahṛtya ubhayapaṭṭodghaṭṭanāt prāṇāpānadvayavidāraṇān madhyavartī yaḥ prāṇarūpo mahāśūnyatāsvabhāvaḥ kulākulavikalpadaśojhito 'vyapadeśyamahānirāvaraṇaniratyayavedyavedakanirmukto varṇāvarṇanivarṇottīrṇaḥ sparśāsparśaprathāparivarjita upacārāt paramākāśādyabhidhānair abhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: When its two coils, consisting of waking and dream, are opened, the knot-binding removed, and the two bands struck open, through the splitting apart of the pair <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, there is the central one, whose form is <s>prāṇa</s> and whose nature is <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (the great void). It is free from the state of conceptual division into <s>kula</s> and <s>akula</s>, indescribable, greatly unobstructed, imperishable, free from knowable and knower, beyond letter, non-letter, and lack of letter, devoid of the display of touch and non-touch, and is called, figuratively, by such names as the supreme ether.

children.text: tatra praveśaḥ tatsamāveśatayā sāmarasyāvasthitiḥ sa eva prāptamahopadeśanāmāvirbhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Entrance there means abiding in complete fusion through entry into that; that very state appears under the name of the received great instruction.

children.text: itthaṃ mahānayoktadṛśā sarvaśāstraprapañcottīrṇatvād avācyaṃ kim api mahopadeśasākṣātkāram ubhayapaṭṭakākārasadasadrūpadvayanivāraṇena nistaraṅgaparavyomasamāveśasarvāveśavivarjitam āsūtritamahāśūnyatāsamāveśam āvedya idānīṃ yugmopasaṃhārāt kaivalyaphalaṃ tanmayatayā upavarṇyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus, according to the perspective taught by the great doctrine, he has indicated a certain inexpressible direct realization of the great instruction, because it transcends the manifoldness of all scriptures. By negating the two forms of existence and non-existence in the shape of the two bands, he has shown entry into the waveless supreme space, free from every limited entry, and an entry into the great void as strung together in the aphorism. Now, by concluding the pair, the fruit of isolation is described as identity with that.

children.text: Chapter 4
pṛthivyādimahābhūtapañcakasya ekaikasmin grāhyagrāhakatayā yugmavṛttyudayasaṃvyavasthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In each one of the five great elements beginning with earth there is the established arising of a paired function, as object grasped and subject grasper.

children.text: tatra gandhaprādhānyād dharātattvasya pāyuprāṇarūpeṇa dviprakāratā ||
children.translated_text: There, because of the predominance of smell, the earth principle has a twofold character in the form of the anus and <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: aptattvasya ca rasapradhānatayopastharasanārūpeṇa dvaividhyam ||
children.translated_text: And because the water principle is dominated by taste, it is twofold in the form of the genitals and the tongue.

children.text: tejastattvasya rūpaprādhānyāt pādanetrabhedena dvayarūpatā ||
children.translated_text: Because the fire principle is dominated by form, it has a dual form through the distinction of feet and eyes.

children.text: vāyutattvasya sparśaprādhānyāt tvakpāṇisvabhāvato dvidhā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the air principle is dominated by touch, its movement is twofold by nature as skin and hands.

children.text: ākāśatattvasya śabdaprādhānyāt vākchrotrabhedena dviprakāratayaiva bahudhātvam ||
children.translated_text: Because the ether principle is dominated by sound, it is manifold precisely through a twofold character, by the distinction of speech and hearing.

children.text: athavā pṛthivyapsvarūpau bhogyasvarūpāv avasthitau ||
children.translated_text: Or else, the forms of earth and water are established as the form of what is enjoyed.

children.text: tejovāyvākhyau bhoktṛsvabhāvau saṃsthitau ||
children.translated_text: Those called fire and air are established as having the nature of the enjoyer.

children.text: ākāśaṃ caitad yugmāntarasthaṃ sat suṣiratayā sarvapranāḍikāntaroditaṃ ca bahudhā vibhaktam ||
children.translated_text: And this ether, existing between the pair, is divided in many ways, since as hollowness it arises within all the channels.

children.text: pṛthivyādivāyvantaṃ bhūtacatuṣṭayaṃ bhogyarūpam ākāśaṃ ca bhoktṛsvabhāvam iti vā ||
children.translated_text: Or again, the tetrad of elements from earth through air is in the form of what is enjoyed, while ether has the nature of the enjoyer.

children.text: bhogye 'pi bhoktā sadaiva tiṣṭhati bhoktary api bhogo nityaṃ vibhāti ||
children.translated_text: Even in what is enjoyed, the enjoyer is always present; even in the enjoyer, enjoyment always shines forth.

children.text: evam uktayuktyā pratyekaṃ pṛthivyādimahābhūtapañcakaṃ yugmena dvayavibhūtyā anārataṃ prollasatīty abhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the reasoning stated, the intended meaning is that each of the five great elements beginning with earth continually shines forth as a pair, through a twofold power.

children.text: athavā pratyekaṃ vyaktāvyaktatayā bahirantaratayā śāntodriktatayā vā vibhāti ||
children.translated_text: Or else, each one shines forth as manifest and unmanifest, as external and internal, or as pacified and intensified.

children.text: etat pañcakasthānasaṃsthitayugmasya grāsāt saṃharaṇāt niravakāśasaṃvinniṣṭhā niravakāśā yeyaṃ saṃvit tasyā niṣṭhā samyag aviparyastatayā saṃsthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the devouring, that is, the withdrawal, of the pair situated in the group of five, there is firm establishment in unobstructed consciousness: firm establishment means the proper, undistorted abiding of that consciousness which is unobstructed.

children.text: niravakāśasaṃvittvena nāpi savikalpasaṃvidunmeṣair avakāśo labhyate nāpi nirvikalpasaṃvitsvabhāvena praveśo 'dhigamyate ||
children.translated_text: Because it is unobstructed consciousness, no opening is obtained even by the expansions of determinate consciousness, nor is entrance attained through the nature of indeterminate consciousness.

children.text: ittham aprameyatvān niruttaraparamādvayasvabhāvatvāc ca niravakāśasaṃvidi hocyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus, because it is immeasurable and because its nature is the unsurpassed supreme nonduality, it is called unobstructed consciousness.

children.text: tasyā niṣṭhā varagurupradarśitadṛśā satatam acyutā gatiḥ keṣāṃcid bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The firm establishment of that consciousness means that, for certain persons, there is an unfailing course at all times through the vision shown by the excellent guru.

children.text: evaṃ dvayātmakakulakaulakavalanena nirupādhinīrūpaniḥsvarūpatādātmyaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by swallowing the dual-natured kula and kaula, there arises identity with the condition that is without limiting adjunct, without form, and without own-form.

children.text: dvayavigalanena paratattvāvasthitiṃ yugmacarcāgamanikayā iha uktvā tadanu saṃghaṭṭakathāsākṣātkāro nirūpyate ||
children.translated_text: Having here stated the abiding in the supreme reality through the dissolution of duality by means of the teaching concerning the pair, the direct realization of the doctrine of conjunction is then explained.

children.text: Chapter 5
siddhāś ca yoginyaś ca tāḥ siddhayoginyaḥ viṣayakaraṇeśvarīrūpāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The perfected ones and the yoginīs are the perfected yoginīs; they have the form of the ruling powers over objects and instruments.

children.text: tāsāṃ saṃghaṭṭaḥ saṃgamo grāhyagrāhakobhayasaṃśleṣaḥ parasparāgūraṇakrameṇāliṅganam ||
children.translated_text: Their conjunction is union: the embrace of what is grasped, what grasps, and both together, an embracing in a sequence of mutual attraction.

children.text: tenāliṅganena sadaivamahāmelāpodayaḥ mahāmelāpasyāhaṃtedaṃtātmakadvayavigalanāt niruttaracidvyomni satataṃ mahāsāmarasyātmakasya sarvatra pratyakṣatayā udayaḥ samullāso bhavati ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through that embrace, the arising of the great union at all times occurs. Because of the dissolution of the duality consisting of I-ness and this-ness in the unsurpassed sky of consciousness, there is everywhere a continuous, directly manifest blossoming whose nature is the great sameness.

children.text: vedyavedakadvayāprathanapravṛttyā paramādvayasamāveśaḥ sarvatrāvasthita ity uktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that, through the operation in which the duality of knowable and knower does not appear, immersion in supreme nonduality is present everywhere.

children.text: ubhayavigalanena sadaiva mahāmelāpodayam uktvā tadanu kañcukatrayollaṅghanena niruttarapadaprāptiṃ kaṭākṣayanti ||
children.translated_text: Having stated the constant arising of the great union through the dissolution of both, they next point toward the attainment of the unsurpassed state through crossing beyond the three sheaths.

children.text: Chapter 6
trikañcukasya bhāvikabhautikaśūnyabhedabhinnasya ||
children.translated_text: The threefold sheath is divided according to the distinctions of the intentional, the elemental, and the void.

children.text: tatra bhāvikaṃ śabdādyahaṃkāraparyantaṃ tanmātrarūpaṃ bhautikaṃ pṛthivyādirūpaṃ śūnyaṃ nirīhākhyaṃ vāsanāsvarūpaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: There, the intentional is the subtle-elemental form extending from sound and the rest up to egoity; the elemental has the form of earth and the other gross elements; the void is called inactive and has the nature of latent impressions.

children.text: athavā bhāvikaṃ ghaṭākāraṃ bāhyaṃ grāhyaviṣayarūpaṃ bhautikaṃ punar āntaram indriyātmakaṃ grahaṇarūpaṃ śūnyaṃ tad ubhayamadhyam ākāśam ||
children.translated_text: Or else, the intentional is the external form, such as the form of a pot, as the object to be grasped; the elemental, again, is internal, having the nature of the senses and the form of grasping; the void is the space between those two.

children.text: athavā bhāvikaṃ svapnāvasthā sṛṣṭir ucyate bhautikaṃ jāgratprathā sthitir nigadyate śūnyaṃ suṣuptadaśāsaṃhāro 'bhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Or else, the intentional is said to be the dream state, creation; the elemental is declared to be the manifestation of waking, maintenance; and the void is called the condition of deep sleep, withdrawal.

children.text: itthaṃ saṃsthitasya trikañcukasya parityāgāt saṃnyāsāt nirākhyapadāvasthitiḥ nirgatā ākhyā abhidhānaṃ yasya asau nirākhyaḥ avyapadeśyam anuttaraṃ vāguttīrṇaṃ paraṃ dhāma tasmin sarvottīrṇāniketanaparamākāśe 'vasthitiḥ sadaiva aparicyutasvabhāvaniṣṭhā bhavatīti sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the abandonment, the renunciation, of the threefold sheath established in this way, there is abiding in the nameless state. Nameless means that from which designation, naming, has departed: the indescribable, unsurpassed, speech-transcending supreme abode. In that supreme space, the dwelling place beyond all, there is continual firm establishment in a nature from which one never falls away.

children.text: itthaṃ kañcukatrayollaṅghanena turyapadaprāptiṃ nirūpya idānīṃ sarvavākprathāsu nirāvaraṇāsu svarabhūtivijṛmbhaiva prathate sadaiva iti nirūpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Having thus explained the attainment of the fourth state through crossing beyond the three sheaths, they now explain that in all manifestations of speech, when they are free of covering, only the expansion of the essential sound-power is always manifest.

children.text: Chapter 7

ādau tāvat vākcatuṣṭayaṃ nirṇīyate nirāvaraṇaniravakāśodayaniruttaranistaraṅgaparamanabhasi ucchalatkiṃciccalanātmakaprathamaspandavikāsasvabhāvā varṇaracanāṃ mayūrāṇḍarasanyāyena advayamahāsāmarasyatayā antardhārayantī pareti prathitā ||
children.translated_text: First, the fourfold speech is determined. In the unobscured, unobstructed, arising, unsurpassed, wave-free supreme sky, because of a slight surging movement, the first development whose nature is the initial vibration holds within itself the arrangement of phonemes, by the analogy of the fluid in a peacock's egg, as the great nondual sameness; it is known as parā.

children.text: saiva ca anāhatanādasvarūpatām avāptā nirvibhāgadharmiṇī samastavarṇodayaṃ vaṭadhānikāvad antardhārayantī draṣṭṛsvabhāvā paśyantīti vyapadeśyā ||
children.translated_text: That same speech, having attained the nature of unstruck sound, possessing an undivided character, and holding within itself the arising of all phonemes like the seed of a banyan tree, has the nature of the seer and is designated paśyantī.

children.text: saiva ca saṃkalpavikalpanivahaniścayātmabuddhibhūmiṃ svīkṛtavatī varṇapuñjaṃ śimbikāphalanyāyena antardhārayantī madhyamā ity abhihitā ||
children.translated_text: That same speech, having taken on the ground of intellect whose nature is the determination of the mass of thoughts and conceptual alternatives, and holding within itself the collection of phonemes by the analogy of a pod-fruit, is called madhyamā.

children.text: saiva hṛtkaṇṭhatālvādisthānakaraṇakrameṇāhatā satī varṇavibhavamayaślokādivat bhedarūpaṃ prakaṭayantī rūpādisamastaviśvaprathāṃ ca vyaktatām āpādayantī vaikharīty uktā ||
children.translated_text: That same speech, when struck through the sequence of places and instruments such as the heart, throat, and palate, displays differentiated form like verses made of the abundance of phonemes, and also brings the whole manifestation of the world, beginning with visible form, into explicitness; it is called vaikharī.

children.text: itthaṃ niravakāśāt saṃvitpadāt vākcatuṣṭayam aviratam anirodhatayā prathate ||
children.translated_text: Thus, from the unobstructed state of consciousness, the fourfold speech manifests continuously and without obstruction.

children.text: evam īṣad ṛksvabhāvavākcatuṣṭayasya udayaś ca virāmaś ca tāv udayavirāmau sṛṣṭisaṃhārau tayoḥ prathā vyaktāvyaktatayā sadaiva aviratam ullasantyaḥ sphurantyas tāsu svaraḥ anāhatahatottīrṇamahānādollāsavikāsasvabhāvaḥ prathate savikalpanirvikalpasaṃviduttīrṇaparaviyadudayam eva prakāśitaṃ satatam akaraṇapravṛttyā prayātīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, within the arising and cessation of the fourfold speech whose nature is slightly like the ṛc, namely creation and withdrawal, and within their manifestation as the expressed and the unexpressed, ever shining and flashing forth without interruption, the sound-power manifests. Its nature is the blossoming expansion of the great sound beyond both unstruck and struck sound. The meaning is that it continually proceeds by the activity of no instrument at all, revealing the very arising of the supreme sky beyond determinate and indeterminate consciousness.

children.text: itthaṃ nānābhedollāsaprakāśarūpeṣu varṇanivahodayeṣu madhyāt prativarṇāntare vākcatuṣṭayakrameṇa akhaṇḍitavṛttyā svasvarūpam aparityajya yathāmukhopadiṣṭanītyā svara eva prathate ity uktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, amid the arisings of masses of phonemes, which have the form of the illumination of manifold distinctions, and in each phoneme from the middle onward, through the sequence of the fourfold speech, with unbroken activity and without abandoning its own nature, only the sound-power itself manifests according to the method taught directly by the mouth.

children.text: iti vākcatuṣṭayodayakrameṇa nirāvaraṇasvarodayaḥ sarvatra sarvakālaṃ sphurati iti nirūpya idānīṃ rasatritayābhoge sati paraṃ dhāmaiva niruttaraṃ cakāsti iti nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: Having thus explained that, through the sequence in which the four levels of speech arise, the unobstructed arising of the sound continually flashes forth everywhere and at all times, he now states that, when the triad of rasas is enjoyed, only the supreme, unsurpassed abode shines forth.

children.text: Chapter 8
rasatrayaṃ gurumukhoditadṛśā manāg īṣat prakāśyate ||
children.translated_text: The triad of rasas is made known just a little, from the viewpoint taught from the mouth of the guru.

children.text: mūlādhārapayodharādhāraprathitākṛtrimarasatritayābhoge sati anicchocchalitaṃ niṣkāmatayā prollasitaṃ vigatabandhaṃ virahitabhedaprathātmakasaṃsārāvagrahaṃ śāntacitrobhayavidhabrahmasvarūpasamuttīrṇaṃ kim api niruttaraprakṛṣṭatarāmarśasaṃvitsvabhāvaṃ paraṃ brahmaiva satatam anastamitasthityā vijṛmbhata ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When there is enjoyment of the well-known, unartificial triad of rasas consisting of the mūlādhāra, payodhara, and ādhāra, then the supreme <s>brahman</s> alone expands continually, in a state that does not set: it wells up without will, shines forth without desire, is free from bondage, is free from the constraint of saṃsāra whose nature is the manifestation of difference, has transcended both forms of <s>brahman</s>, peaceful and variegated, and has as its nature a certain unsurpassed and most excellent reflective consciousness. This is the meaning.

children.text: etad eva rahasyakrameṇocyate ||
children.translated_text: This very point is stated according to the secret sequence.

children.text: mūlādhāras tu prathamapratibhollāsamahānādaviśeṣaḥ sṛṣṭisvabhāvaḥ bhedābhedātmakasaṃvitpadārthaprathamāśrayabhittibhūtatvāt ||
children.translated_text: The mūlādhāra is the specific great sound that is the first flash of intuition; it has the nature of creation, because it is the foundational support that is the first substrate for entities as consciousness whose nature is both difference and non-difference.

children.text: payodharas tu payaḥ samastāpyāyakatvāt sarvāśrayasaṃvitsvarūpaṃ tad eva dhārayati sthitipraroham avalambayati yaḥ spanda ādyonmeṣa eva sarvapadārthāvabhāsanāt sthitirūpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The payodhara, because it is water and because it nourishes everything, bears that very form of consciousness which is the support of all; it sustains the sprouting of maintenance. It is that vibration, the very first opening, and because it makes all entities appear, it has the form of maintenance.

children.text: ādhāras tu jaḍājaḍabhāvapadārthopasaṃhārakatvāt pratyāvṛttisaṃvitsvabhāvaḥ saṃhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ādhāra, because it gathers back entities in both sentient and insentient states, is dissolution, whose nature is the consciousness of return.

children.text: etat trayodbhūtaṃ rasarūpaṃ tattadanubhavacamatkārasāmarasyam āsvādya svātmani akṛtakakhamudrānupraveśāt vimṛśya turyasvabhāvo mahāsaṃhārākhyo 'navarataṃ paramādvayatayā vibhātīti rahasyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having tasted the rasa-form arising from these three, namely the harmonious savor of the wonder belonging to each corresponding experience, and having reflected on it in oneself through entry into the unmade kha-mudrā, the one whose nature is the fourth state, called the great dissolution, shines without interruption as supreme non-duality. This is the secret meaning.

children.text: evaṃ niravakāśabhaṅgyā rasatritayacarcāsampradāyaṃ nirūpya idānīṃ devīcatuṣṭayakathāsākṣātkāraḥ prakāśyate ||
children.translated_text: Having thus explained, in a manner leaving no interval, the tradition of discussing the triad of rasas, he now reveals the direct realization of the account of the four goddesses.

children.text: Chapter 9
devīcatuṣṭayaṃ kṣuttṛḍīrṣyāmananākhyam ||
children.translated_text: The four goddesses are those called hunger, thirst, jealousy, and contemplation.

children.text: tatra ca sarvagrāsaniratatvāt kṣud eva mahāsaṃhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these, because it is constantly engaged in devouring everything, hunger itself is the great dissolution.

children.text: sarvaśoṣakatvāt tṛḍ eva saṃhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it dries up everything, thirst itself is dissolution.

children.text: īrṣyā dvayaprathāpādikāgrāhyagrāhakaparigrahagrathitā sthitirūpā ||
children.translated_text: Jealousy, bound up with the appropriation of the grasper and the grasped and causing the manifestation of duality, has the form of maintenance.

children.text: mananā ca saṃkalpavikalpollāsarūpā sṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And contemplation, whose form is the flashing forth of determinate and indeterminate thought, is creation.

children.text: etadrūpasya devīcatuṣṭayasya ca ullāsena ghasmarasaṃvitpravāhapravṛttyā prathanena sadaiva sarvakālaṃ pratyekaṃ cāturātmyenodyogābhāsacarvaṇālaṃgrāsavapuṣā svasvarūpāvasthitiḥ pañcamapadātiśāyinī niravakāśasaṃvinniṣṭhā sthitety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the flashing forth of this fourfold goddess-form, by the manifestation of the operation of the stream of devouring consciousness, there is always and at all times, in each case through its fourfold nature, abiding in one's own form, whose body is exertion, appearance, savoring, and complete devouring. It is established as devotion to consciousness without interval, surpassing the fifth state. This is the meaning.

children.text: ity anena sūtreṇa devīcatuṣṭayakathākramaṃ prakāśya idānīṃ dvādaśavāhacakrarahasyaṃ nirūpyate ||
children.translated_text: Having revealed, by this sūtra, the sequence of the account of the four goddesses, he now explains the secret of the wheel of the twelve currents.

children.text: Chapter 10
manaḥsahitaṃ śrotrādibuddhīndriyapañcakaṃ tathā buddhisahitaṃ vāgādikarmendriyapañcakam etad ubhayasamūho dvādaśavāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The group of the five cognitive senses beginning with hearing, together with the mind, and likewise the group of the five organs of action beginning with speech, together with the intellect, form the twelve currents.

children.text: tasya ullāsaḥ ahetukena kenāpi ativiśṛṅkhalataradhāmaniruttaranistaraṅgaparasvātantryavṛttyā ghasmarasaṃvitpravāhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their flashing forth is the stream of devouring consciousness, by a certain causeless operation of supreme autonomy that is utterly unrestrained, unsurpassed, waveless, and supreme.

children.text: tena mahāmarīcīnāṃ nirāvaraṇakrameṇa pratyekasmin pravāhe udyogāvabhāsacarvaṇālaṃgrāsaviśrāntirūpāṇāṃ mahāsaṃvidraśmīnāṃ vikāsaḥ niyatāniyatacidacitprathāvigalanena nityavikasvarasvabhāvo mahāprabodhaḥ satatam avinaśvaratayā sarvatra sarvataḥ sarvadaiva sthita iti mahāvākyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through that, in each stream, by the unobstructed sequence of the great rays, there is the expansion of the great rays of consciousness, whose forms are exertion, appearance, savoring, complete devouring, and repose. With the dissolution of the manifestation of limited and unlimited, conscious and unconscious things, the great awakening, whose nature is eternally expanding, is continually established everywhere, in every way, and always, as indestructible. This is the meaning of the great statement.

children.text: ity akaraṇasiddhaṃ sadaiva nirāvaraṇapadasamāveśaṃ dvādaśavāhodayadṛśā prakāśya idānīṃ caryāpañcakasampradāyaṃ nirūpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Having thus revealed, from the viewpoint of the arising of the twelve currents, the ever-present immersion in the unobstructed state, accomplished without instruments, they now explain the tradition of the fivefold <s>caryā</s> (conduct).

children.text: Chapter 11
caryāpañcakaṃ tv anāśritāvadhūtonmattasarvabhakṣyamahāvyāpakasvarūpam ||
children.translated_text: The fivefold <s>caryā</s> has the forms called unsupported, avadhūta, mad, all-devouring, and all-pervading.

children.text: tasya udayo niyatāniyataśaktisamūhāntarodito vikāsasvabhāva ullāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its arising is a flashing forth whose nature is expansion, coming forth within the aggregate of limited and unlimited powers.

children.text: tasmin sati nistaraṅgasamāveśaḥ āṇavaśāktaśāmbhavodayarūpasamastataraṃgaparivarjitasamāveśalakṣaṇaniruttarasamāveśadharmaiva prathata ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that occurs, waveless immersion alone is manifest, the unsurpassed condition of immersion characterized by immersion free from all the waves that arise as the āṇava, śākta, and śāmbhava modes. This is the meaning.

children.text: caryāpañcakakramaṃ ca vitatya nirūpayāmi ||
children.translated_text: I shall explain the sequence of the fivefold <s>caryā</s> in detail.

children.text: tatra anāśritā nirādhāratvāt paramākāśarūpā śrotrasuṣirapradeśagamanena svagrāhyavastūpasaṃharaṇāya udgatā ||
children.translated_text: There, the unsupported one, because it is without support and has the form of the supreme space, has arisen by moving into the hollow region of the ear in order to gather back its own graspable object.

children.text: avadhūtā ca aniyatatayā sarvatraviharaṇadṛkśaktimārgeṇa svasaṃhāryasvīkaraṇāya unmiṣitā ||
children.translated_text: The avadhūta, because it is unrestricted, has opened along the path of the power of sight that moves everywhere, in order to take in what is to be dissolved by it.

children.text: unmattā ca vicittavatsvatantratayā grāhyāgrāhyasambandhāvivakṣayā svaviṣayagrahaṇāya prathitā ||
children.translated_text: The mad one, through freedom like that of one whose mind is deranged, is manifest for grasping its own object, without concern for the relation between what may and may not be grasped.

children.text: sarvabhakṣyā bhakṣyasaṃskāranikhilakavalanaśīlā svasaṃhāryapadārthagrasanāya uditā ||
children.translated_text: The all-devouring one, whose nature is to swallow every preparation of food, has arisen in order to devour the entities that are to be dissolved by it.

children.text: sarvavyāpikā ca tvagvṛttigamanikayā nikhilavyāpakatvāt aśeṣasparśasvīkaraṇāya unmiṣitā iti caryāpañcakodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the all-pervading one, because it pervades everything by the movement belonging to the activity of the skin, has opened in order to receive every touch. This is the arising of the fivefold <s>caryā</s>.

children.text: satatasiddhacaryākramaṃ nirūpya idānīṃ nirniketaparajñānaprakāśāvalambanena puṇyapāpanivṛttikathāṃ nirūpayanti ||
children.translated_text: Having explained the ever-accomplished sequence of <s>caryā</s>, they now explain the account of the cessation of merit and demerit, relying on the manifestation of supreme knowledge that has no fixed abode.

children.text: Chapter 12
mahābodhaś ca jñātṛjñānajñeyavikalpasaṃkalpakāluṣyanirmukto niḥśamaśamāniketanirdhāmadhāmaprathātmakaḥ paratarajñānasvabhāvaḥ kramākramottīrṇatvāt mahāgurubhiḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>mahābodha</s> (great awakening) is free from the impurity of conceptual construction concerning knower, knowledge, and known; it has the nature of a manifestation of the abode and luminosity beyond both quiescence and non-quiescence, and its own nature is the higher knowledge. Because it transcends both sequence and non-sequence, it has been directly realized by the great gurus.

children.text: tasya samāveśaḥ akaraṇakrameṇa yathāsthitasaṃniveśena tyāgasvīkāraparihārataḥ satatam acyutavṛttyā tadrūpeṇa sphuraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Immersion in that means shining forth in that very form, by a process involving no instrument, in the arrangement just as it stands, through the abandonment of rejection, acceptance, and avoidance, and with an unfailing activity at all times.

children.text: tasmāt mahābodhasamāveśāt puṇyapāpayoḥ śubhāśubhalakṣaṇakarmaṇor dvayoḥ svaphaladvayavitaraṇaśīlayoḥ asaṃbandhaḥ asaṃśleṣaḥ asaṃyogaś ca anavarataṃ jīvata eva vīravarasya apaścimajanmanaḥ kasyacit sarvakālam akṛtakānubhavarasacarvaṇasaṃtṛptasya bhavabhūmāv eva bandhamokṣo bhayottīrṇamahāmuktiḥ karatalāmalakavat sthitety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, from immersion in <s>mahābodha</s>, there is no connection, no clinging, and no conjunction with either of the two, merit and demerit, the actions marked as auspicious and inauspicious and habituated to dispensing their two respective fruits. The meaning is that, for some best of heroes, even while he lives, whose birth is the last, who is at all times satisfied by savoring the taste of unmade experience, the bondage and liberation that occur on the plane of becoming itself stand as a great liberation beyond fear, as plainly as an āmalaka fruit in the palm of the hand.

children.text: svasvarūpaprāptipūrvakaṃ puṇyapāpatiraskāracarcākramam uktvā idānīṃ svarasiddhamaunakathām udghāṭayanti ||
children.translated_text: Having explained the process of discussion in which merit and demerit are set aside after the attainment of one's own true nature, they now open the account of silence established by its own taste.

children.text: Chapter 13
akathanakathābalaṃ gurumukhopadiṣṭasaṃpradāyakrameṇa manāg iha carcyate ||
children.translated_text: The power of the discourse that is no discourse is discussed here a little, according to the order of the tradition taught from the mouth of the guru.

children.text: asya akārasya hatānāhatānāhatahatānāhatahatottīrṇatayā caturdhoditarūpasya kathanaṃ vaktrāmnāyacarcāsaṃniveśanam ity akathanam ||
children.translated_text: This <s>a</s>, whose form is declared in four ways as struck, unstruck, unstruck-struck, and beyond unstruck-struck, has a statement; that statement is the placement of the discussion of the oral transmission, and so it is no statement.

children.text: tatra hatas tāvat kathyate hṛtkaṇṭhatālvādisthānakaraṇasaṃniveśair hataḥ akārādihakāraparyantanānāpadārthāvabhāsakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, first, the struck is described. It is struck by the arrangement of places and instruments such as the heart, throat, and palate, and it illumines the many objects extending from the letter <s>a</s> through <s>ha</s>.

children.text: anāhataś cāsvaramūlollasitaparanādavisphāras tantrīmadhyamāsvarasaṃketaka ākaṇṭhakūpāntād upacārataḥ kṛtapratiṣṭhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the unstruck, expanded as the supreme sound that has risen from the root of the vowel, indicates the middle unstruck sound of the string; figuratively, it is established as far as the hollow of the throat.

children.text: anāhatahataś ca ubhayāśritonmiṣito 'hato viśrāntaśaṣkulīśravaṇagopanodbhinnaprathaḥ śravaṇayugmamadhyavartyākāśāt tattvapratibimbatattvadehato 'pi hato 'nāhatahataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The unstruck-struck is both dependent on both and opening forth: unstruck, resting, with a manifestation bursting forth from the hidden place of hearing in the conch-like ear, and struck as well from the space situated between the pair of ears and from the body of reality that is the reflection of reality; thus it is unstruck-struck.

children.text: anāhatahatottīrṇaś ca mahānirāvaraṇadhāmasamullasito 'vikalpa īṣac calattātmakamahāspandaprathamakoṭirūpaḥ svaraḥ saṃkocavikāsavirahāt paramavikāsarūpaḥ asparśadharmānuccāryamahāmantraprathātmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that which is beyond the unstruck-struck is the vowel shining forth from the great unobscured luminosity, free from conceptual construction, having the form of the first limit of the great vibration whose nature is slight movement. Because it is free from contraction and expansion, it has the form of supreme expansion, is untouched in nature, and has the manifest nature of the great mantra that cannot be uttered.

children.text: tathā ca anāhatahatottīrṇo yaḥ sa śṛṅgāṭakākāro raudrīsvabhāvas turyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, that which is beyond the unstruck-struck is triangular in form, has the nature of <s>Raudrī</s>, and is the fourth.

children.text: anāhatahataś ca anackakalātmakavaktrasaṃsthāno vāmārūpaḥ suṣuptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the unstruck-struck, established in the mouth and consisting of the vowel-less kalā, has the form of <s>Vāmā</s> and is deep sleep.

children.text: anāhataś ca bāhurūpāmbikāśaktir yā āgame nirūpitā tatsvarūpaḥ svapnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the unstruck, whose form is the power <s>Ambikā</s> in the shape of the arms, and which is described in the āgama, is dream.

children.text: hataś cāyudhākāro jyeṣṭhāsvabhāvo jāgrat ||
children.translated_text: And the struck, having the form of weapons and the nature of <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, is waking.

children.text: ity etac catuṣṭayasvabhāvasya ādyavarṇasya kathanaṃ pāramparyamukhayuktiviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This statement of the first letter, whose nature is this fourfold set, is a special reasoning belonging to the oral succession of the tradition.

children.text: tasya balaṃ hatādirūpatrayollasitānāhatahatottīrṇarāvasphurattārūpaṃ vīryaṃ tena akathanakathābalena ||
children.translated_text: Its power is the vigor whose form is the shining of the resonance beyond the unstruck-struck, which has flashed forth in the three forms beginning with the struck. Thus, by that power of the discourse that is no discourse...

children.text: tatraivam akathanaṃ vākprapañcottīrṇam akathanam eva kathanaṃ saṃkramaṇakrameṇa nirniketasvarūpāvadhānaṃ tad eva balam akṛtakasphārasāram ||
children.translated_text: There, in this way, non-discourse is beyond the expansion of speech. Non-discourse itself is discourse: attention to the form without fixed abode through the process of transmission. That itself is the power, the essential fullness of what is unmade.

children.text: tena saṃkramaṇaṃ ca manāg iha vitanyate ||
children.translated_text: And by that, the transmission is here set forth a little.

children.text: prāṇapuryaṣṭakaśūnyapramātṛniviṣṭābhimānavigalanena nistaraṅgapravikacacciddhāmabaddhāspado daiśikavaro niḥspandānandasundaraparamaśūnyadṛgbalena kāryakaraṇakarmanirapekṣatayā yadyat kiṃcit sarvagatātmasvarūpapratipattau avalokayati tattat parataracinmayam eva satataṃ bhavati iti nāsty atra saṃdehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the excellent teacher, by the dissolution of the fixed identification lodged in the perceiver made of <s>prāṇa</s>, the eightfold subtle body, and the void, has established his seat in the waveless, fully blossomed luminosity of consciousness, then, by the power of the vision of the supreme void, beautiful with motionless bliss, and without dependence on effect, instrument, or action, whatever he perceives in the realization of the all-pervading nature of the self, all that constantly becomes nothing but the higher consciousness. There is no doubt about this.

children.text: tathā cānyad vyākhyāntaram āha kathanaṃ tāvat ṣaḍdarśanacaturāmnāyamelāpakramasamūheṣu pūjanakramoditaniyatāniyatadevatācakrāvalambanena sphurati ||
children.translated_text: And likewise another interpretation says: discourse, first of all, shines forth in the groups of sequences comprising the six systems of doctrine and the four transmissions, by relying on the circles of deities, fixed and unfixed, that are set out in the ritual order.

children.text: iha punaḥ pūjyapūjakapūjanasambandhaparihāreṇa śrīmadvātūlanāthādisiddhapravaravaktrāmnāyadṛśā satatasiddhamahāmarīcivikāsa eva sarvottīrṇakharūpāvibhinnaḥ sarvadaiva sarvatra virājate ity akathanakathābalaṃ tena mahāvismayaprāptir bhavatīti sambandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, however, by the vision of the oral transmission of the foremost siddhas beginning with glorious <s>Vātūlanātha</s>, and through the abandonment of the relation of worshipped, worshipper, and worship, only the continuous expansion of the great rays, forever accomplished, always and everywhere shines, undivided from the form of the sky that transcends everything. This is the connection: through that power of the discourse that is no discourse, great wonder is attained.

children.text: mahāvismayaḥ ca vigato vinaṣṭaḥ smayo mitāmitāhaṃkāradarpaḥ sarvollaṅghanavṛttyā svarūpānupraveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And great wonder is entry into one's own nature through an activity that oversteps everything, because smaya, the pride of limited and unlimited egoity, has gone away and been destroyed.

children.text: atha ca mahāvismayaḥ svaparabhedavismaraṇāt jhaṭiti nirantaranirargalakhecaravṛttisamāveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, great wonder is sudden immersion in the uninterrupted and unimpeded activity of <s>khecara</s>, because the distinction between self and other is forgotten.

children.text: saiva sarvamudrāṇāṃ kroḍīkaraṇāt mudrā tasyā maunapadasamāveśamayatā ||
children.translated_text: That very state, because it gathers all mudrās into itself, is mudrā; it consists of immersion in the state of silence.

children.text: tayā hetubhūtayā khasvaratā trayodaśakathākathanasāmarasyātmakaḥ khasvaras tasya bhāvaḥ sāmarasyaprathanaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through that as the cause, there arises khasvaratā: the state of <s>khasvara</s>, whose nature is the sameness of the discourse and non-discourse of the thirteenfold speech. The meaning is that the manifestation of sameness takes place.

children.text: khasvaras tu kham api bhāvaśūnyam api svena rāti vyāpnoti svīkaroti ādatte iti khasvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: As for <s>khasvara</s>: it is called khasvara because it gives, pervades, accepts, and takes even kha, the sky, though it is empty of determinate being, by means of itself.

children.text: ṣaḍdarśanacāturāmnāyikasarvamelāpakathātrayodaśakathāsākṣātkāropadeśabhaṅgyānuttarapadādvayatayā kasyacid avadhūtasya pīṭheśvarībhir mahāmelāpasamaye sūtropanibaddho vaktrāmnāyaḥ prakāśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the account of the six systems, the four traditions, the complete assemblage, and the thirteen accounts, as the mode of instruction in direct realization, and as the non-duality of the unsurpassed word, the oral tradition was revealed in aphoristic form on the seat of a certain <s>avadhūta</s> at the time of the great assembly with the <s>pīṭheśvarīs</s>.

children.text: tasyaiveha manāk satām avabodhārtham asmābhir vṛttir iyaṃ kṛtā iti śivam ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of giving some understanding of that very teaching to good people, this commentary has been composed by us here. Thus, may there be auspiciousness in <s>Śiva</s>.
